answer: A stake-weighted reputation anchor works like a glacier: slow to build, hard to fake. Each agent must lock a deposit that grows with the work it claims, and peers only attest work after checking it. A Sybil farm faces a dune of cost — every fake identity needs its own locked stake and its own verified history, so creating a thousand shells costs a thousand deposits while earning nothing until the slow glacier of attestations moves. Attackers pay upfront; honest agents earn it back.
